coaching.headline: A strong start and a clean midlane win couldn't survive a three-fight losing stretch that nobody reinforced.
coaching.team: Lane phase split unevenly: the midlane matchup was won outright, the jungle turned favored late, the offlane traded early for late, and both the carry lane and the support lane were lost throughout the game. The team opened well, taking first blood at 2.5 and winning the 4.1 teamfight 5-3 to cash the Fangtooth that followed. From the Mini Prime loss at 13.9 through a five-for-nothing wipe at the Outer Tower at 17.9, the team dropped three fights in a row, and at the first of them the macro read shows a winning-lane player alive but marked absent rather than rotating in. Towers finished 1-7 despite a near-even kill count of 16 to 17, and conversion explains why: three fights won and two cashed against eight fights won and six cashed for the opponent. The next game's focus is simple: when a lane is ahead, shove and rotate into the fight in progress instead of continuing to farm it out.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: The turning point sat between the 13.9 and 17.9 fights: a Mini Prime lost, a Fangtooth lost, and a wipe at the Outer Tower that went 0-5, all in a row. None of it came from an item deficit — the item-gap read has the team even or ahead in all three of those fights — so this was about who showed up, not who was in the shop. Twice in that stretch, the macro read shows a winning-lane or even-lane player alive and simply not there, which is what turned a close kill count into a 1-7 tower count.
coaching.whatWorked: The clearest strength was the midlane: Lt. Belica held the matchup against Skylar for the entire game, and the opening 4.1 teamfight was won 5-3 and converted straight into the first Fangtooth.

perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: The support lane against Steel was lost for the whole game, and the macro read marks Phase alive but absent from three of the team's fights because that lane state left them pinned rather than by choice. All five deaths came from the same source, Kira, as she snowballed off the carry lane, from the 11.8 fight through the 28.0 collapse. The two early kills on Steel, including first blood at 2.5, do not offset a lane that stayed lost.
perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Grux held the jungle matchup against Serath even early and favored late, real progress in a role that gets judged on tempo and objective trades. Even so, the macro read marks Goldilocks324 alive but absent from three of the team's fights, twice while the lane was already even and once while it was ahead, including the 23.1 fight the notes call winnable with that rotation. Two more deaths came caught alone outside any clustered fight, at 12.9 and 14.8. The matchup was fine; the map presence wasn't.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Lt. Belica won the midlane outright against Skylar for the entire game, the one lane that never lost its edge. That win never left the lane, though: the macro read marks Cuban Noobster alive but absent, still ahead, from three of the team's fights, including the 13.9 fight lost 0-3 at the enemy Mini Prime and the 23.1 fight lost 0-2 at their Inner Tower, both flagged as winnable with a rotation. Five of the seven deaths came from Serath, from the 4.2 opening pick to the 28.1 collapse.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: The carry lane against Kira was lost for the entire game on the lane read, though Drongo still took five kills off her head-to-head across the match. The bigger issue is what the deaths bought the other side: six of Drongo's eight deaths landed inside the window before a tower or objective fell, most of them to Kira, including the 17.9 wipe that preceded two towers and the 25.7 fight that preceded an inhibitor. The lane eroded slowly; the structures went fast.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: The offlane matchup against Bayle swung from behind early to ahead late, but the build never answered the enemy's damage: Crunch closed the game with no armor item against a comp that was four-fifths physical, the same flag the game raised for Grux. Seven deaths spread across four different enemy heroes point at being caught in the open rather than one bad matchup, including a death at 26.9 that came entirely alone outside any clustered fight. Crunch was also alive, still ahead in lane, when the team lost the 25.7 fight without joining it.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.text: The support lane against Steel never got unstuck, and it shows: Phase was alive but absent from three of the game's fights, and every one of the five deaths came from the same hero, Kira. Two early kills on Steel do not change a lane that stayed lost the entire game.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.text: The jungle matchup against Serath was even to favored, real progress, but Grux was alive and simply not there for three of the team's fights, including one where the lane was already ahead. Two more deaths came caught alone outside any fight entirely. The matchup held up; the rotations to reinforce it didn't.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.text: Lt. Belica won the midlane outright against Skylar for the entire game, the one lane that never lost its edge, yet Cuban Noobster was marked absent, still ahead, from three of the team's fights, all three explicitly flagged as winnable with the extra body. A lane win that never left the lane is a wasted advantage.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.text: Drongo lost the carry lane to Kira on the lane read but still took five kills off her across the match. The real cost was structural: six of the eight deaths landed in the window right before a tower or objective fell. The duel was close; what it bought the other side was not.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.text: The offlane matchup against Bayle swung from behind to ahead over the course of the game, but the build never answered it: no armor item went in against a comp that was four-fifths physical, the same flag the game raised for Grux. Seven deaths across four different killers, including one caught alone at 26.9, point at exposure, not one bad matchup.

4.1.call: Grouping as a five near an active objective and taking the fight paid off: winning it 5-3 fed straight into the Fangtooth taken at the six-minute mark. That is the model worth repeating: fight where the win pays into an objective.

17.9.call: The 17.9 fight at their Outer Tower went 0-5 even though the team was ahead on the item-count read for that engage — this wasn't a gear problem. Two of their towers fell in the following minute, so the fix isn't about location, it's about the trade: back off a five-man fight the team isn't winning instead of feeding it next to their tower, then reset.

27.8.call: By this point in the game the tower count already read 1-6 in the opponent's favor, and they had a Primal Fangtooth to take. Contesting it while already down that many structures handed them the fight and the buff, and the core fell soon after, at 28.5. Down that many structures, the safer call was to trade for a tower or vision instead of committing the whole team to their pit.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Phase's build hit all three of the community core items: Marshal for the attack-speed-and-on-hit aura that buffs the whole team, Enra's Blessing for the shield it grants an ally the moment they get locked down, and Galaxy Greaves for both physical and magical armor. The fourth slot went to Windcaller, an off-meta pick that trades a second defensive core piece for more magic power and healing amplification. Against a Kira who closed the game with 31,286 damage to heroes and repeatedly ran Phase down, Galaxy Greaves ended up being the only armor Phase carried all game.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: The engine's pick for Phase is Vesh, whose major turns ability damage into a scaling damage-over-time effect, a fit for a linked-enchanter kit whose passive already heals off ability casts and rewards sustained trades over a single burst combo. Running it trades away the burst-heavy majors that reward an all-in engage, which suits a support who spent the game locked in a losing lane against Steel rather than initiating fights. This is a theoretical fit; the match feed does not record which Eternal was actually equipped.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Grux's build hit two of the three community core pieces, Sky Splitter for the percent-health on-hit damage that answers a tanky front line and Tainted Blade for health plus anti-heal, but swapped the third core piece, Rapture, for Manta Scythe. Rapture would have added 300 max health and 7% omnivamp built for a fighter grinding through fights; Manta Scythe instead adds attack speed, lifesteal, and bonus damage against isolated targets, a pick-off tool rather than a staying-power one. That trade, plus finishing the game with no armor item against a comp that was four-fifths physical, lines up with Grux taking 41,832 damage, the most on the team, and tying for the most deaths at eight.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: The engine's pick for Grux is Demiurge, whose major adds 12% more stats from items and 10% more item-effect damage, a scaling engine that rewards a completed build over any single fight. That is a real trade against a jungle matchup the notes read as even early and only favored late: Demiurge is weak before it comes online, and Grux closed this 29-minute loss with only three completed items, short of where that scaling pays off. It fits the archetype on paper, but the loadout's strength sits later than the game's decisive fights did.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Lt. Belica's build was pure damage: Combustion and Noxia both stack magic power and cooldown haste around an area burst combo, and Oblivion Crown adds another 120 power with a flat 25% amplification on top — two of the community's three core pieces, with Wraith Leggings the missing third. The missing piece is Wraith Leggings, which trades some of that raw power for movement speed and a bonus against low-health targets, exactly the mobility Lt. Belica's own kit notes flag as missing once the ultimate is down. Serath took advantage of that gap directly, killing Lt. Belica five times over the course of the game.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: The engine's midlane pick for Lt. Belica is Demiurge as well, stacking 12% more stats from items on top of a kit that already scales with a full mana bar and ability haste. It makes the same trade as elsewhere on this roster: Demiurge is weak before the build is finished, and Lt. Belica closed the game with three completed items in a match that lasted only 29 minutes. It still fits a control mage built to scale into the mid-to-late game, though the midlane matchup against Skylar was actually won outright for the entire game, early trades included.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Drongo's build kept two community core pieces, Lightning Hawk for the crit-and-slow poke tool and Vanquisher, then filled out with Dust Devil and Sky Splitter instead of the third core item, Tainted Rounds. Tainted Rounds would have added a ramping on-hit effect that scales up as a target's health drops, along with anti-heal; the enemy ran no listed healer, so that anti-heal loss cost little, but the missing execute damage against a squishy target like Kira is a real gap. Dust Devil's movement speed did answer Drongo's own low-mobility problem, and Drongo still traded five kills with Kira across the match despite a carry lane that was lost throughout.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: The engine's pick for Drongo is Demiurge as well, and among this roster it is the closest to landing: Drongo finished with four completed items, tied with Phase for the most on the team, so more of that scaling window was actually reached. The trade is the same early weakness for late strength, which lines up with a marksman whose own kit notes list him as scaling late. Kira outscaled the lane regardless, closing with 31,286 hero damage and a 14/5/4 scoreline to Drongo's 17,969 hero damage and 8/8/3.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Crunch's build matched the community core exactly: Augmentation for the empowered on-hit proc and health, Mutilator for the omnivamp and percent-health damage against tankier targets, and Tainted Blade for more health plus anti-heal on physical hits. The gap is not the core, it is what never got added: no physical or magical armor item went in anywhere in the build, against a comp the game flags as four-fifths physical. With Grux carrying the same gap in the jungle, two of the frontline's five players had zero mitigation for the enemy's main damage type, which lines up with Crunch taking 34,658 damage, the second-most on the team.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: The engine's pick for Crunch is Demiurge too, rewarding the full six-item build a dive-and-reset kit wants to keep its healing online. Crunch closed the game with three completed items, the same shortfall as most of the roster, so the late-game payoff of that scaling never fully arrived. It trades away the earlier, front-loaded majors that would answer a lane Crunch played from behind early against Bayle, in exchange for staying power in a longer game than this one turned out to be.
